page_title: STAR Programme - Student Transition and Residential
content: The Student Transition and Residential (STAR) programme is a free, 3-day summer residential event hosted annually by the University of Central Lancashire (UCLan) in August, before the start of Semester 1. It is specially designed for incoming undergraduate offer-holders who have declared a disability, specific learning difficulty (such as dyslexia or dyspraxia), mental health condition, or who are care-experienced or estranged students. The programme provides an early, gentle introduction to university life before the campus becomes busy during Welcome Week.

page_title: STAR Programme - Student Transition and Residential
content: Participation in the STAR programme is completely free of charge. Eligible offer-holders receive free accommodation for two nights in UCLan student halls of residence on the Preston campus. All meals (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) and refreshments are provided throughout the 3-day event. Students stay in single student rooms, allowing them to experience hall living, practice using electronic door keys, test kitchen spaces, and familiarise themselves with the accommodation layout before September.

page_title: STAR Programme - Student Transition and Residential
content: The STAR programme is run in partnership with trained Student Wellbeing Ambassadors (SWAs). Ambassadors are current UCLan students who provide friendly, informal peer mentoring. They meet attendees upon arrival, guide small-group campus and library orientation walks, host fun evening social activities (such as board game nights, crafts, and campus scavenger hunts), and answer practical questions about university routines, student budgets, and making friends. Ambassadors are available throughout the residential to ensure no student feels alone.

page_title: STAR Programme - Student Transition and Residential
section: Pre-programme Online Sessions and Facebook Community
content: Ahead of the 3-day residential in August, UCLan runs online transition webinars on Microsoft Teams where students can meet the Inclusive Support team and Student Wellbeing Ambassadors from home. Attendees are also invited to join a dedicated, moderated STAR Facebook group where offer-holders can introduce themselves, chat with peers on their course, and ask questions about packing, student life, and transport.

page_title: STAR Programme - Student Transition and Residential
section: Can Parents, Carers, or Personal Assistants Attend?
content: Parents and carers are warmly invited to attend the arrival welcome session and introductory briefing on Day 1 of the STAR programme. However, the overnight residential and evening student activities are exclusively for participating students so they can build peer independence. If a student requires a registered Personal Assistant (PA) or overnight carer for medical or accessibility reasons, UCLan arranges an adjacent room in halls at no cost; please inform the Inclusive Support team when booking.

The UCLan Inclusive Support team supports students with a wide range of declared conditions, including physical disabilities, sensory impairments (visual or hearing), neurodiversity (such as dyslexia, dyspraxia, ADHD, and autism), mental health conditions, and chronic medical illnesses (such as diabetes, epilepsy, Crohn's, or chronic fatigue). Support is confidential, tailored to individual needs, and free to all enrolled students and offer-holders.

section: Inclusive Support Plans (ISP) and Reasonable Adjustments
content: An Inclusive Support Plan (ISP) is an agreed official document outlining the reasonable adjustments recommended for a student during their course. Adjustments can include 25% extra time in timed exams, separate quiet exam rooms, permission to record lectures, assignment extensions, assistive technology software, and lecture slides provided at least 24 hours in advance. An ISP is created during a 1-to-1 appointment with an Inclusive Support Advisor and is shared with academic tutors only with the student's consent.

section: Screening and Assessments for Dyslexia and Dyspraxia
content: If you suspect you have a specific learning difficulty such as dyslexia or dyspraxia but have never had a formal diagnosis, UCLan's Inclusive Support team provides free initial screening. If the screening suggests an assessment is warranted, the team helps arrange a full diagnostic assessment with a certified educational psychologist. UCLan often subsidizes assessment fees for students experiencing financial hardship.

Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA) is a UK government grant provided through Student Finance (such as Student Finance England, Wales, Northern Ireland, or SAAS) to cover study-related costs arising from a mental health condition, long-term illness, or disability. DSA is not a loan and does not need to be repaid. It does not depend on household income. It can fund specialist software (such as text-to-speech or mind-mapping), ergonomic equipment, one-to-one specialist study skills tuition, and assistive technology training.

section: How to Apply for DSA with UCLan's Support
content: To apply for DSA, students submit a DSA1 form online via their Student Finance portal along with supporting medical evidence (e.g., a doctor's letter, hospital report, or diagnostic assessment report). Once eligibility is confirmed, the student attends a Study Needs Assessment to discuss personalized equipment and support. The UCLan Inclusive Support team can assist you at every stage of the application and help upload medical evidence.

The UCLan Mental Health and Wellbeing Service provides free, confidential support for all enrolled students. Support options include one-to-one wellbeing advisor appointments, mental health practitioner guidance, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), counseling, and wellbeing workshops. Appointments can be booked through the Starfish platform or by visiting the Student Centre on the Preston campus. Contact the team at wellbeing@uclan.ac.uk or call 01772 893020.

If you or another student is experiencing a mental health crisis, severe distress, or emergency, please reach out to professional human support immediately: On-campus security is available 24/7 on 01772 892068 (or dial 999 for emergency services). Off-campus NHS mental health urgent support is available 24/7 by calling NHS 111. Free confidential listening is available 24/7 via Samaritans on 116 123, or text SHOUT to 85258. For under-35s in distress, call Papyrus HOPELINE247 on 0800 068 4141. The university wellbeing team is available during office hours on 01772 893020 or wellbeing@uclan.ac.uk.

page_title: Student Accommodation and Halls of Residence
section: Accessible and Adapted Rooms in University Halls
content: UCLan provides adapted rooms in student accommodation for students with physical or sensory requirements. Features include wheelchair-accessible bedrooms, roll-in wet rooms, low-level kitchen counters, flashing fire alarms (Deaf Alerter systems), vibrator pads for beds, and automatic push-button doors. Offer-holders needing adapted rooms should declare their requirements early on the accommodation application portal so the accommodation team can match suitable halls.

page_title: Student Accommodation and Halls of Residence
section: Early Arrival for STAR Attendees and Disabled Students
content: Students who participate in the STAR programme or who have an Inclusive Support Plan may request an early arrival date before Welcome Week officially begins. This allows disabled students to unpack calmly, explore their flat and kitchen, meet flatmates gradually, and settle into halls before the large campus crowds arrive in September. Early arrival requests can be arranged via the Student Accommodation Service.

section: Student Centre Services and Starfish Portal
content: The Student Centre on the Preston campus is the central physical hub for all student enquiries. Here you can find help with student ID cards, tuition fees, council tax exemption certificates, registration confirmation, and career advice. UCLan uses an online student portal called Starfish, which allows students to view their academic advisor, schedule appointments with Inclusive Support and Wellbeing, and connect with academic tutors easily from their phone or laptop.

WISER is UCLan's specialist academic skills development service. Located in the Library and Student Hub, WISER offers free one-to-one tutorials, group workshops, and online learning modules on academic writing, critical thinking, dissertation planning, mathematics and statistics, and referencing (including Harvard and APA styles). WISER works closely with Inclusive Support to support neurodivergent students with academic essay organization.

Welcome Week takes place during the third week of September. During Welcome Week, students complete their in-person identity verification to collect their student ID card, attend course induction sessions, join clubs and societies at the Freshers' Fair, and attend campus orientation tours. Students who completed the STAR programme in August can fast-track their registration and meet up again with their Student Wellbeing Ambassadors.

section: Support for International Students with Disabilities
content: International offer-holders with disabilities or learning difficulties are fully eligible to access UCLan's Inclusive Support, Wellbeing Service, and the STAR programme. While UK government Disabled Students' Allowance (DSA) is restricted to UK residents, UCLan provides internal institutional funding and equipment loans so international disabled students receive equivalent reasonable adjustments, including exam accommodations and assistive software. Free academic English language classes are also provided.
